description: def t; yield(1); end; a = 1; t { |x| a = a + x }; a + 1 : Int -- the boundary case for capIntact, and the reason it compares *types* rather than forbidding assignment. The block really does mutate a captured local, and that is fine because it leaves the type alone: same shape as class-setter-method for ivars. Sits next to xc-block-retypes-capture on purpose -- the two differ only in the assigned type.
sorbet_note: Method `t` uses `yield` but does not mention a block parameter
